title: AI for Recruitment: What's Actually Changing
description: A practical, honest look at how AI is reshaping recruitment and job hunting in 2026 — from the recruiter's stack to the candidate's resume. Real tools, real bias risks, no hype.

posts.topicTitle: The AI-Powered Recruiter's Stack in 2026: Tools That Actually Work
posts.topicBrief: A practical roundup of the AI tools modern recruiters actually use day-to-day. Cover the core categories: sourcing (hireEZ, Fetcher, Gem), screening and conversational AI (Paradox), end-to-end talent intelligence (Eightfold, Beamery), and outreach (LinkedIn Recruiter AI). Include pricing tiers where available, what each does well, and what to avoid. Be honest about which tools are hype vs which deliver. Target audience: HR leaders, in-house recruiters, agency recruiters.

posts.topicTitle: AI Resume Screening: Honest Pros, Real Bias Risks
posts.topicBrief: Deep-analysis post on AI resume screening. Cover how it actually works (NLP + ML on parsed resume data), the productivity wins (recruiters cite 60-70%% time savings on initial screening), and the very real bias risks. Specifically address: Amazon's 2018 scrapped AI hiring tool case study, the NYC AEDT bias audit law (effective 2023), EEOC's 2023 guidance on AI employment tools, and the EU AI Act's classification of HR AI as high-risk. End with practical guidance: what to audit before deploying, what disclosures to give candidates.

posts.topicTitle: AI Candidate Sourcing vs Boolean Search: When Each Wins
posts.topicBrief: How-to guide comparing traditional boolean LinkedIn/Google sourcing with AI-driven candidate matching (hireEZ, SeekOut, Eightfold). Show concrete examples: a boolean string for 'senior backend engineer with Rust experience in Berlin' vs how the same intent gets handled by AI sourcing tools. Explain when AI matching wins (large talent pools, fuzzy requirements, passive candidates) and when boolean still wins (precise niche roles, security clearances, exact tool experience). Include time-to-shortlist comparisons from real recruiter case studies if available.

posts.topicTitle: AI Tools That Help Recruiters Write Better LinkedIn Posts (Without Sounding Like Job-Board Copy)
posts.topicBrief: Skipped 2026-06-05. Original brief was rewritten in PR #45 (2026-06-02) to deliberately push Klinchapp as the recommended tool — a conversion-bridge strategy that has since been reversed. Generated post (ai-tools-recruiters-linkedin-posts.mdx) was deleted because the result was structurally a product pitch dressed as editorial. Series stays as 7 posts but this order is now unfilled.

posts.topicTitle: How to Write Employer-Brand LinkedIn Posts That Don't Sound Like Corporate PR
posts.topicBrief: Step-by-step guide for recruiters writing employer-brand LinkedIn content that actually earns engagement. Cover: identifying what to write about (team moments, hiring wins, culture truths — not corporate puff), choosing a voice that matches the company's real personality, structuring each post (hook + specific story or detail + invitation to engage), formatting for LinkedIn skimming (short paragraphs, white space), and sustaining a posting cadence without burning out. Editorial in tone — describe practical techniques and the principles behind them. Do not recommend or position any specific product or tool.

posts.topicTitle: AI Resume Builders That Actually Beat ATS in 2026
posts.topicBrief: Tool review flipping perspective from recruiter to candidate. Cover the real AI resume tools: Rezi, Teal, Jobscan, Enhancv, Kickresume, plus the AI rewriters built into LinkedIn (Premium) and Indeed. Explain what ATS systems (Workday, Greenhouse, Lever, iCIMS) actually parse and how AI resume tools claim to optimize for that. Be honest about limitations — these tools help with keyword matching and formatting, but cannot fake fit. Include concrete tips: how to use ChatGPT/Claude to tailor a resume to a specific job description (the prompt structure), what to avoid (over-stuffed keywords), and the new 'human-in-loop' approach that works best.

posts.topicTitle: Will AI Replace Recruiters? An Honest Analysis
posts.topicBrief: Opinion piece taking a clear position: AI will not replace recruiters, but it will replace the recruiters who don't use AI. Build the argument with specifics. What AI handles well today (sourcing, screening, scheduling, FAQ — the high-volume low-judgment work). What AI is still bad at (assessing executive-level fit, navigating compensation negotiation, reading organizational politics during placement, building long-term candidate relationships). Cite real data on recruiter headcount trends — LinkedIn's 2025 Future of Recruiting report is a good source. End with a practical takeaway: the skills recruiters should develop now to stay essential, and what employers should be hiring recruiters FOR in 2026.
